questions.problem:
The temperature of a certain liquid under heating is given by the function $T(t),$ where $t$ is the time in hours. The values of $T(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| **$t$** | $1.2$ | $1.4$ | $1.6$ | $1.8$ | $2.0$ | $2.2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T(t)$ | $-12$ | $-10$ | $-4$ | $6$ | $10$ | $13$ |

$$

$$

Determine the instantaneous temperature rate at the instant of time $t=1.6$ using a central difference approximation with the step size $h=0.2.$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{T}^{′}(t)≈\frac{T(t+h)-T(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=1.6$ with step size $h=0.2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(1.6) & ≈\frac{T(1.6+0.2)-T(1.6-0.2)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{T(1.8)-T(1.4)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{6-(-10)}{0.4} \\  & =\frac{16}{0.4} \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous temperature rate at the instant of time $t=1.6$ is ${40}^{∘}$ per hour.

questions.problem:
Sam wanted to estimate the rate of weight growth of his new puppy. He took note of its weight every week, for $7$ weeks. The results are shown in the table below, where $W(t)$ is the puppy's weight (measured in pounds) after $t$ weeks from birth.

| **$t$** | $8$ | $9$ | $10$ | $11$ | $12$ | $13$ | $14$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $W(t)$ | $9$ | $10.1$ | $11.3$ | $12.4$ | $13.5$ | $14.6$ | $15.8$ |

$$

$$

Approximate the puppy's rate of weight growth $12$ weeks after birth using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{W}^{′}(t)≈\frac{W(t+h)-W(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=12$ and step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{W}^{′}(0.2) & ≈\frac{W(12+1)-W(12-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{W(13)-W(11)}{2} \\  & =\frac{14.6-12.4}{2} \\  & =\frac{2.2}{2} \\  & =1.1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the rate of weight growth at the instant of time $t=12$ is $1.1\,\text{lb}/\text{week}.$

questions.problem:
In an environmental study, the water level in a reservoir (in $m$) after $t$ hours is given by the function $W(t).$ The values of $W(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| **$t$** | $0.8$ | $1.0$ | $1.2$ | $1.4$ | $1.6$ | $1.8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **$W(t)$** | $5.6$ | $5.3$ | $5.0$ | $4.7$ | $4.2$ | $3.9$ |

Approximate the reservoir’s water level's instantaneous rate of change at $t=1.4$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=0.2.$

The reservoir’s water level at $t=1.4$ is decreasing at approximately 
{{field-1}} $m$ per hour.
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{W}^{′}(t)≈\frac{W(t+h)-W(t-h)}{2h},
$$

at time $t=1.4$ with step size $h=0.2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{W}^{′}(1.4) & ≈\frac{W(1.4+0.2)-W(1.4-0.2)}{2(0.2)} \\  & =\frac{W(1.6)-W(1.2)}{0.4} \\  & =\frac{4.2-5.0}{0.4} \\  & =\frac{-0.8}{0.4} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the reservoir’s water level at $t=1.4$ is decreasing at approximately $2\,m$ per hour.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **$C(t)$** | $12.4$ | $11.8$ | $11.0$ | $10.4$ | $9.8$ | $9.2$ |

Approximate the drug’s concentration instantaneous rate of change at $t=3.2$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=0.4.$

The drug’s concentration at $t=3.2$ is decreasing at approximately 
{{field-1}} $mg/L$ per hour.
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{C}^{′}(t)≈\frac{C(t+h)-C(t-h)}{2h},
$$

at time $t=3.2$ with step size $h=0.4.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{′}(3.2) & ≈\frac{C(3.2+0.4)-C(3.2-0.4)}{2(0.4)} \\  & =\frac{C(3.6)-C(2.8)}{0.8} \\  & =\frac{9.8-11.0}{0.8} \\  & =\frac{(-1.2)}{0.8} \\  & =-1.5.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
In a lab experiment, the temperature of a chemical reactor (in ${}^{∘}C$) after $t$ minutes is given by the function $T(t).$ The values of $T(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| **$t$** | $1.2$ | $1.6$ | $2.0$ | $2.4$ | $2.8$ | $3.2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **$T(t)$** | $28$ | $30$ | $32$ | $34$ | $35$ | $36$ |

Approximate the reactor’s temperature instantaneous rate of change at $t=2.0$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=0.4.$

The reactor’s temperature at $t=2.0$ is changing at approximately 
{{field-1}} ${}^{∘}C$ per minute.
questions.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{T}^{′}(t)≈\frac{T(t+h)-T(t-h)}{2h},
$$

at time $t=2.0$ with step size $h=0.4.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(2.0) & ≈\frac{T(2.0+0.4)-T(2.0-0.4)}{2(0.4)} \\  & =\frac{T(2.4)-T(1.6)}{0.8} \\  & =\frac{34-30}{0.8} \\  & =\frac{4}{0.8} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
